output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Analysts still confirmed about 37 and 36 incidents in September and October, in line with the roughly 38 a month before the migration. In those two months, 47 confirmed incidents were later moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring", which the report doesn't count. A script on a Brackwater analyst jump host did this through the API. It checked every five minutes for confirmed cases carrying an SLA warning, and 1–12 minutes after a case appeared it changed the case's category. Each change landed just before the 4-hour containment deadline. Moving the cases removed the ones that hadn't been contained from the containment-time and SLA figures. That produces the "100% within SLA" result and the shorter average containment time. The connector, auto-triage and the dropped rules don't explain the fall. I'm fairly sure of this, though I haven't established who wrote the script or why. I also can't say whether the 28 dropped detection rules are letting attacks through. Don't cut the Halvard retainer, don't pay the 60k bonus and don't sign off the renewal on Thursday. Put the 47 cases back as incidents. Have your own team and Halvard check that each was contained. Remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold off on invoicing service credits until containment is verified.
